comment: Films from the owner's own phone, scored by tools/video_regression/run_recognition.py only (counting is not scored here). The films are local, never committed.

movementWindows.label: walking to the bar and jumping up
pull-ups: two calibration reps, then five
squats with the hands behind the head

scenarios.notes: The owner's own recording of one Cindy round at the gym, the camera's HUD burned in, 77.7 s, 720x1280. The film stays out of git: keep it at tests/fixtures/owner/rec-a.mp4 (ignored). Windows and reps are read off the per-frame joint signal, never off contact sheets: pull-up tops are the peaks of the nose height (7 reps, the first two being the app's calibration reps), push-up and squat bottoms are the troughs of the nose height (10 push-ups, 16 squats), walks and the walk-in are the stretches with no set. The squats are done with the hands behind the head, so the wrists stay above the shoulders; the HUD counted 14 of 15 at 64.7 s, the signal shows 16 troughs.

movementWindows.label: setting the phone down and walking in
five pull-ups: two calibration reps, then three
dropping off the bar and picking the phone up

scenarios.notes: The owner's own recording of the start of a Cindy round at the gym, the HUD burned in, 37.8 s, 720x1280: a finger over the lens, the walk in, five pull-ups (the HUD reads 1 of 2 and then 3 of 5, so the first two are calibration reps), then the athlete drops off the bar and the clip ends. Local only, at tests/fixtures/owner/rec-b.mp4 (ignored). The five rep times are the peaks of the nose height; a sixth peak at 17.6 s is the dead hang after the jump up, not a rep.
